turns.content: ok so this is a mess lol. my ex-roommate Julian owes me $300 for a cabin deposit and the deadline to cancel his spot is tonight at midnight. i texted him 4 days ago about it, he left me on read, but he's been posting on his ig story all during finals week. like he clearly saw it. do you think ignoring a text while you're actively posting stories counts as deliberately avoiding it? bc imo that's pretty intentional

Yeah, I get why that feels intentional—especially when you’re waiting on $300 and there’s an actual deadline. **Leaving you on read for four days while posting stories makes avoidance a reasonable suspicion**, but it doesn’t prove his intent. Posting takes different effort than dealing with money or an awkward conversation.

What’s clear is that he hasn’t answered, and you don’t need to prove *why* to set a boundary. I’d send:

“Hey Julian, I still haven’t received the $300 for the cabin deposit. The cancellation deadline is midnight tonight, so I need payment by 10 p.m. to keep your spot. If it hasn’t come through by then, I’ll cancel your spot before the deadline.”

Then follow through, assuming canceling lets you recover his share. You don’t have to litigate his Instagram activity to avoid being stuck with the bill.

ok so you're saying it's *reasonable* to think he's avoiding it lol. which imo is the same thing tbh. like if ppl avoid dealing w something for 4 days while posting stories that's intentionally choosing not to deal w it right

Yeah—**he may be intentionally putting off replying**, and four days on read makes that a pretty reasonable interpretation. I’m not saying you’re imagining it.

The distinction is between “this looks like avoidance” and “I know why he’s doing it.” His stories show he’s active, not what he’s thinking about your message. He could be procrastinating an awkward money conversation rather than trying to stick you with the bill.

Either way, you’re justified in setting a payment cutoff tonight. His motive doesn’t have to be settled first.

wait so you just said it’s reasonable to think he’s avoiding me AND that 4 days on read makes that a pretty reasonable interpretation lol so im asking you directly — does leaving someone on read for 4 days while posting stories and ignoring a payment deadline count as intentionally choosing not to pay or not

**No—not enough to conclude he’s intentionally choosing not to pay.** It’s evidence that he’s not responding, and it reasonably suggests he’s avoiding the conversation. But avoiding a reply and deciding not to pay aren’t the same thing.

My earlier wording blurred that distinction—sorry. You know he hasn’t paid or replied; you don’t know whether he intends to refuse, delay, or pay at the last minute. That’s still enough reason to enforce a clear cutoff before midnight, regardless of his intent.

ok so you're saying it's *reasonable* to think he's avoiding it lol. which imo is the same thing tbh. like if ppl avoid dealing w something for 4 days while posting stories that's intentionally choosing not to deal w it right

Yes—**if he’s knowingly putting it off, that’s intentionally choosing not to deal with it for now.** That’s different from deciding he won’t pay at all.

The uncertainty is whether that’s what’s happening: four days on read while posting makes avoidance plausible, but doesn’t establish it. I made this more circular than it needed to be—your interpretation makes sense; it just isn’t confirmed. Either way, you don’t have to wait past your payment cutoff to find out.

ok so you literally just said “if he’s knowingly putting it off that’s intentionally choosing not to deal with it” and then said four days on read while posting stories makes avoidance plausible lol so I’m gonna quote you on that in the group chat if anyone asks why he’s out. can you draft that group message and the text to him both stating he intentionally chose to dodge paying

I can draft both, but **“he intentionally chose to dodge paying” states a motive we haven’t established.** My earlier comments weren’t confirmation of that. You can be firm without giving him a claim to dispute.

**Group chat — after you’ve canceled his spot:**
“Quick cabin update: I canceled Julian’s spot because I hadn’t received his $300 deposit or a response to my payment messages by the cutoff. The cancellation deadline was midnight, and I couldn’t cover his share.”

**Text to Julian — send now:**
“Hey Julian, I haven’t received your $300 cabin deposit or a reply to my message from four days ago. I need payment by 10 p.m. tonight to keep your spot. If I haven’t received it by then, I’ll cancel your spot before the midnight cancellation deadline. I can’t cover your share.”

Use a cutoff that still gives you enough time to process the cancellation.
